title: Scripture and Tradition
definition: The doctrine of Scripture and tradition teaches that church tradition may be useful when faithful to Scripture, but it must never stand above or against the Word of God.
summary: The church benefits from faithful teachers, creeds, confessions, historical theology, and wise counsel. Yet every tradition must be tested by Scripture. The Bible remains the final authority for doctrine and practice.
christFocus: Jesus rebuked traditions that nullified the Word of God and fulfilled the Scriptures as the final revelation of God's redemptive plan. True tradition serves Christ only when it submits to Scripture.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Tradition can preserve helpful teaching, but it is not equal to Scripture. A faithful church honors the wisdom of past believers while testing all things by God's written Word.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Some traditions can help discipleship, worship, and doctrine. Others can obscure the Gospel, bind consciences, or replace obedience to God with human customs.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive faithful teaching with gratitude, but test everything by Scripture. Do not reject history arrogantly, and do not accept tradition blindly.
